name: Hailey-Hailey Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnosis of Hailey-Hailey Disease

criteria.description: Recurrent vesicles and erosions primarily in intertriginous areas (axillae, groin, neck folds)
Acantholysis with a 'dilapidated brick wall' appearance on skin biopsy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent vesiculopustular eruptions in intertriginous regions
Acantholysis with 'dilapidated brick wall' histological pattern

common.symptomName: Painful erosions and fissures in skin folds

occasional.symptomName: Hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation in healed areas
Exacerbation with heat, sweating, or friction

rare.symptomName: Eczema herpeticum secondary to viral infection
Extensive widespread blistering beyond typical folds

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing suprabasal acantholysis with 'dilapidated brick wall' appearance
genetic: Mutation in ATP2C1 gene encoding the secretory pathway Ca2+/Mn2+-ATPase (SPCA1)
other: Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Positive direct immunofluorescence with intercellular IgG and C3
Transient papulovesicular eruption usually in older men
Histology shows focal acantholysis without familial pattern

redFlags: Rapidly spreading blistering beyond typical intertriginous areas
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis from secondary bacterial infection
Severe pain or functional impairment due to extensive erosions
references: Hailey-Hailey disease: clinical features, pathogenesis, and management. Dermatol Clin. 2019.
ATP2C1 mutations in Hailey-Hailey disease. J Invest Dermatol. 2018.
Hailey-Hailey disease: a review of clinical features and treatment options. Am J Clin Dermatol. 2020.
